QUOTE: Binary detection runs before parsing. Non-text files are skipped, but there is no size limit, so a large generated `.c` is still read.
VERDICT: MISS
WHY: The answer mentions binary detection, but it doesn't say the filter drops files whose extension lies about them. It also says doxygen's default patterns handle extensions and never mentions the parse-built front end claiming file types doxygen can't read. It doesn't state the "resolved scope is not the whole answer" idea with one of the two named filters.
